items.title: Step 1
items.description:
In this workshop, you will create a recipe tracker using JavaScript objects.

Start by creating an empty array named `recipes`. This is the array you'll push the recipe objects into later.

hints.text: You should create an array named `recipes`.
Your `recipes` array should be empty.

items.title: Step 2
items.description:
Create an object named `recipe1`. Inside the `recipe1` object, create a `name` property with the value `"Spaghetti Carbonara"`.

Also inside the `recipe1` object, create an `ingredients` property with an array as the value. The array should have `spaghetti`, `Parmesan cheese`, `pancetta`, and `black pepper` inside it.

hints.text: You should create an object named `recipe1`.
Your `recipe1` object should have a `name` property.
Your `name` property should be set to `Spaghetti Carbonara`.
Your `recipe1` object should have an `ingredients` property.
Your `ingredients` property should have an array value.
The array value of your `ingredients` property should have `spaghetti`, `Parmesan cheese`, `pancetta`, and `black pepper` in it.

items.title: Step 3
items.description:
Add the following properties to the `recipe1` object:

| Key | Value   |
| ----------- | ------- |
|`cookingTime`|`22`|
|`totalIngredients`|`null`|
|`difficultyLevel`|`""`|

The properties with `null` and empty string values will be updated later after you calculate them.

hints.text: Your `recipe1` object should have a `cookingTime` property.
Your `cookingTime` property should be set to `22`.
Your `recipe1` object should have a `totalIngredients` property.
Your `totalIngredients` property should be set to `null`.
Your `recipe1` object should have a `difficultyLevel` property.
Your `difficultyLevel` property should be set to an empty string.

items.title: Step 6
items.description:
Before you move on, you should practice how to access properties from an object.

You can use either dot (`.`) or bracket (`[]`) notation to do this. Here's an example:

```js
const person = {
  name: "John",
  age: 30,
  job: "Software Engineer"
};

console.log(person.name); // John
console.log(person['age']);  // 30
```

Access the `name` property of `recipe1`, and assign it to the variable `recipe1Name`.

Next, access the `cookingTime` property of `recipe2` and assign it to the variable `recipe2CookingTime`.

Finally, access the `ingredients` property of `recipe3` and assign it to the variable `recipe3Ingredients`.

Make sure all the variables you created are logged to the console.

hints.text: You should create a `recipe1Name` variable.
You should assign the value of the `name` property of `recipe1` to your `recipe1Name` variable.
You should log `recipe1Name` to the console.
You should create a `recipe2CookingTime` variable.
You should assign the value of the `cookingTime` property of `recipe2` to your `recipe2CookingTime` variable.
You should log `recipe2CookingTime` to the console.
You should create a `recipe3Ingredients` variable.
You should assign the value of the `ingredients` property of `recipe3` to your `recipe3Ingredients` variable.
You should log `recipe3Ingredients` to the console.

items.title: Step 7
items.description:
You should now push the three objects into the `recipes` array. To do this, you can use the `push()` method.

Use the `push()` method to push all the recipe objects into the `recipes` array. Make sure to push `recipe1`, `recipe2`, and `recipe3` in that order.

Also delete the `recipe1Name`, `recipe2CookingTime` and `recipe3Ingredients` variables, and the `console.log` statements which log those variables.

hints.text: You should push all the recipe objects into the `recipes` array. Make sure to push them in the order they are declared.
You should remove the `recipe1Name` variable.
You should remove the `console.log(recipe1Name);` statement.
You should remove the `recipe2CookingTime` variable.
You should remove the `console.log(recipe2CookingTime);` statement.
You should remove the `recipe3Ingredients` variable.
You should remove the `console.log(recipe3Ingredients);` statement.

items.title: Step 8
items.description: Create a `getTotalIngredients` function that takes a single argument, representing an array with ingredients, and returns the number of ingredients from the array passed to the function.

hints.text: You should create a `getTotalIngredients` function.
Your `getTotalIngredients` function should have a single parameter.
Your `getTotalIngredients` function should return a number.
`getTotalIngredients(recipe1.ingredients)` should return `4`.
`getTotalIngredients(recipe2.ingredients)` should return `5`.
`getTotalIngredients(recipe3.ingredients)` should return `3`.

items.title: Step 9
items.description:
Create a `getDifficultyLevel` function that takes a number indicating the cooking time as a parameter.

If the cooking time is less than or equal to `30`, the function should return `"easy"`. If it is less than or equal to `60`, the function should return `"medium"`. Otherwise, the function should return `"hard"`.

hints.text: You should create a `getDifficultyLevel` function.
Your `getDifficultyLevel` function should have a single parameter.
Your `getDifficultyLevel` function should return `"easy"` when the cooking time is less than or equal to `30`.
Your `getDifficultyLevel` function should return `"medium"` when the cooking time is greater than `30` and less than or equal to `60`.
Your `getDifficultyLevel` function should return `"hard"` when the cooking time is greater than `60`.

items.title: Step 10
items.description:
It's time to test each of the functions. You can use any of the recipes for this, but this tutorial will start with `recipe1`.

Create two new variables: `recipe1TotalIngredients` and `recipe1DifficultyLevel`. Assign them the values by calling the corresponding function for each variable and passing in the appropriate `recipe1` property.

Finally, log each variable to the console to see the results.

hints.text: You should create a `recipe1TotalIngredients` variable.
Your `recipe1TotalIngredients` variable should be set to `getTotalIngredients(recipe1.ingredients)`.
You should log `recipe1TotalIngredients` to the console.
You should create a `recipe1DifficultyLevel` variable.
Your `recipe1DifficultyLevel` variable should be set to `getDifficultyLevel(recipe1.cookingTime)`.
You should log `recipe1DifficultyLevel` to the console.

items.title: Step 11
items.description:
You can now fill in each item of the `recipes` array with values for the `totalIngredients` and `difficultyLevel` properties.

For now, access the `totalIngredients` and `difficultyLevel` of `recipe1` and set them to the appropriate results of function calls and arguments.

hints.text: You should access the `totalIngredients` property of `recipe1`.
You should assign the result of calling `getTotalIngredients` with `recipe1.ingredients` to the `totalIngredients` property of `recipe1`.
You should access the `difficultyLevel` property of `recipe1`.
You should assign the result of calling `getDifficultyLevel` with `recipe1.cookingTime` to the `difficultyLevel` property of `recipe1`.

items.title: Step 12
items.description: Repeat the process for the `totalIngredients` and `difficultyLevel` properties of `recipe2` and `recipe3`.

hints.text: You should access the `totalIngredients` property of `recipe2`.
You should assign the result of calling `getTotalIngredients` with `recipe2.ingredients` to the `totalIngredients` property of `recipe2`.
You should access the `difficultyLevel` property of `recipe2`.
You should assign the result of calling `getDifficultyLevel` with `recipe2.cookingTime` to the `difficultyLevel` property of `recipe2`.
You should access the `totalIngredients` property of `recipe3`.
You should assign the result of calling `getTotalIngredients` with `recipe3.ingredients` to the `totalIngredients` property of `recipe3`.
You should access the `difficultyLevel` property of `recipe3`.
You should assign the result of calling `getDifficultyLevel` with `recipe3.cookingTime` to the `difficultyLevel` property of `recipe3`.

items.title: Step 13
items.description:
Now, log the `recipes` array to the console to see all its items filled with the updated values.

With that, your recipes tracker project is complete.

hints.text: You should log the `recipes` array to the console.
